correctness.rationale: Every legal rectangle corresponds bijectively to one pair of disjoint edges. For two distinct cycles all 4ab pairs merge. Within a cycle the two alternating 1-factors yield k or 2k nonconsecutive split pairs according to equal/unequal split sizes, while k(k-2) mixed-factor pairs preserve one cycle. This exhausts moves; the matrix degree and projected probabilities follow for all n>=2. Labelled bipartite cycle counts yield the multiplicity formula. Uniform reversible rectangle selection implies the conditioned Ewens(1/2) stationary distribution, with irreducibility from Ryser. The two separately implemented exhaustive verifiers check every state through n=6, and are embedded as executable source, not presumed from external logs.

value.rationale: The classical rectangular-switch sampler on fixed margins is a canonical high-dimensional chain. A genuinely Markovian observable is not automatic; exact strong lumpability to integer partitions yields complete transition rates for all dimensions and an explicitly reversible reduced chain. In particular its full all-n merge/split/stay kernel, conditional Ewens equilibrium, and exact 4-state n=6 example are mathematically motivated and permit reduced-state analysis without large labelled-matrix enumerations. This exceeds routine state counting and does not rely on claiming known totals as new.
